structural: The requirement prescribes the structure of `OllamaConfig` as a `#[non_exhaustive]` struct with five public fields (`model`, `endpoint`, `api_key_env`, `api_key`, `options`), their exact types, five builder signatures, and the Clone, Debug, Deserialize, PartialEq and Serialize implementations. The review roots cover all of it.

- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/config.rs#struct[OllamaConfig]` is `#[non_exhaustive]` and declares the five fields with the prescribed types: `String`, `Option<String>`, `Option<String>`, `Option<SecretString>` and `BTreeMap<String, OptionValue>`. It derives `Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize`, which supplies all five required trait implementations. The derives are on the struct, so no separate impl root is needed. The serde attributes only choose the serialized form, and the text does not constrain that form.
- `impl[OllamaConfig]#1/fn[new]` has the signature `new(model: String) -> Self`. It sets `model` and leaves the optional fields `None` and `options` empty.
- `impl[OllamaConfig]#1/fn[endpoint]` has the signature `endpoint(self, endpoint: String) -> Self`. It sets `Some(endpoint)`.
- `impl[OllamaConfig]#1/fn[api_key_env]` has the signature `api_key_env(self, api_key_env: String) -> Self`. It sets `Some(api_key_env)`.
- `impl[OllamaConfig]#1/fn[api_key]` has the signature `api_key(self, api_key: SecretString) -> Self`. It sets `Some(api_key)`.
- `impl[OllamaConfig]#1/fn[option]` has the signature `option(self, key: String, value: OptionValue) -> Self`. It inserts the pair into `options`.

The prose about what the model, endpoint and credentials configure describes how a consumer uses the config. It is behavioral, so it adds no structural obligation for these roots. I found no structural obligation without a root and no gap.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each observable obligation of `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.OllamaConfig`.

- **Constructor and builders.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/config.rs#mod[tests]/fn[backend_builders_set_only_the_requested_fields]` checks that `OllamaConfig::new` serializes to only `{"model": ...}`. It then chains `endpoint`, `api_key_env`, `api_key` and `option` (with a repeated key overridden, `a` becoming 2). It asserts the full JSON: model, endpoint, api_key_env, api_key and options `{a:2,b:true}`. This shows each builder sets only its own field and that a later option value replaces an earlier one.
- **Serde round trip.** `all_backends_preserve_nested_settings_and_credentials` deserializes an ollama config with `api_key_env` and options. It re-serializes to the same value and round-trips through a string, comparing with `assert_eq` on `AgentConfig`. This exercises `Serialize`, `Deserialize` and `PartialEq` for `OllamaConfig`.
- **Endpoint, credentials, defaults.** `option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic` covers three cases:
  - The default endpoint is `http://localhost:11434`, and no key resolves to `None`.
  - A missing `api_key_env` produces an error that names the variable, and an explicit `api_key` resolves to the explicit value.
  - Non-finite option values are rejected through `options_json`.
- **Configuring requests to the server.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[supplied_ollama_backend_delivers_tools_and_results_over_native_chat]` supplies a real `OllamaConfig` with a custom endpoint, `api_key` and the option `num_predict` against a local server. It asserts that:
  - requests go to `POST /api/chat` on the supplied endpoint;
  - the request carries a bearer authorization header with the key;
  - the request body has `model` equal to `local-ollama` and `options.num_predict` equal to 256.
- **Struct shape and exports.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks the public export inventory.
- **Trait impls.** `Clone` and `Debug` are plain derives with no behavior of their own, so they need no separate test. The `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]` on the struct matches the listed impls.

I found no obligation that is missing a test or assertion.

text: `model` names the model on the Ollama server. The endpoint, credentials, and inference options configure requests to that server.
pub fn endpoint(self, endpoint: String) -> Self;
pub fn api_key_env(self, api_key_env: String) -> Self;
pub fn api_key(self, api_key: SecretString) -> Self;
pub fn option(self, key: String, value: OptionValue) -> Self;
